barriers.pass_condition: Consensus score among team panelists meets or exceeds hire recommendation threshold.

specimens.label: Panel tally, as submitted

lines.text: Panelist 1 — collaboration 4, communication 4: hire
Panelist 2 — collaboration 4, communication 3: hire
Panelist 3 — collaboration 3, communication 2: no hire
Consensus threshold: unanimous, or manager override.
Outcome: not aligned.

specimens.reading: The gate is not an average, it is a veto rule. One dissent and a unanimity requirement produce the same result as three dissents.

barriers.title: Compensation & Leveling Reconciliation
barriers.content:
# Compensation & Leveling Reconciliation

Internal alignment between candidate expected compensation/level and company pay bands / leveling grid.

### Pass Condition
Candidate expectations fit within approved salary band and equity guidelines for the target grade.
barriers.description: Internal alignment between candidate expected compensation/level and company pay bands / leveling grid.
barriers.pass_condition: Candidate expectations fit within approved salary band and equity guidelines for the target grade.

specimens.label: Levelling reconciliation sheet

lines.text: Candidate expectation: 90k · Approved band for L4: 68–79k · Approved band for L5: 84–98k
Panel levelled the candidate at L4.
Gap: 11k above the top of the approved band. Options: level up (needs VP approval), reduce expectation, or close.

specimens.reading: Two independent decisions — a level and a band — meet here for the first time. Neither was visible to the candidate while they were being made.

barriers.title: Headcount & Executive Budget Approval
barriers.content:
# Headcount & Executive Budget Approval

Formal sign-off by department leadership, finance, and talent committee to commit budget for the written offer.

### Pass Condition
Active headcount requisition is formally certified and unblocked by financial leadership.
barriers.description: Formal sign-off by department leadership, finance, and talent committee to commit budget for the written offer.
barriers.pass_condition: Active headcount requisition is formally certified and unblocked by financial leadership.

specimens.label: Approval chain

lines.text: Hiring manager: approved
Director: approved
Finance: pending — quarterly review in progress
Talent committee: blocked on finance
Offer cannot be issued while any step is pending.

specimens.reading: Everyone the candidate met has already said yes. This gate is the reason a process can stop after a unanimous panel.

barriers.title: Reference & Background Verification
barriers.content:
# Reference & Background Verification

Third-party or internal verification of past employment records, academic degrees, and professional references.

### Pass Condition
All mandatory background checks clear with no unresolved factual discrepancies.
barriers.description: Third-party or internal verification of past employment records, academic degrees, and professional references.
barriers.pass_condition: All mandatory background checks clear with no unresolved factual discrepancies.

specimens.label: Verification report

lines.text: Employment record 1 of 3: dates confirmed
Employment record 2 of 3: vendor has Mar 2019–Jun 2021, application states Jan 2019–Aug 2021 — DISCREPANCY
Degree: confirmed · References: 2 of 2 returned, both positive
Offer held pending reconciliation.

specimens.reading: The gate is checking a third-party record against a claim. A mismatch here is usually a document problem with a named remedy, not a finding about honesty.

barriers.title: Offer Closing & Contract Execution
barriers.content:
# Offer Closing & Contract Execution

Final mutual execution of the formal employment agreement and start-date confirmation.

### Pass Condition
Both parties sign offer contract and onboarding workflow is triggered.
barriers.description: Final mutual execution of the formal employment agreement and start-date confirmation.
barriers.pass_condition: Both parties sign offer contract and onboarding workflow is triggered.

specimens.label: Closing sequence

lines.text: Contract issued for signature
Candidate signed
Countersignature pending
Start date confirmed · onboarding workflow triggered

specimens.reading: A signature from one side is not the gate. Until the countersignature lands the requisition is still open, which is where a late freeze can reach it.

mechanisms.title: Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall
mechanisms.content:
# Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall

The candidate’s verified technical execution or domain depth does not meet the established baseline for the role level.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `candidate`
- **Nature:** `rule`
- **Removability:** `candidate`

### Non-Inferences
- Rejection does not mean the candidate has no engineering ability, only that the requirement bar was unmet for this specific benchmark.
mechanisms.summary: The candidate’s verified technical execution or domain depth does not meet the established baseline for the role level.

specimens.label: Feedback naming the gap
specimens.subject: Feedback — technical round

lines.text: The panel was positive on communication and on how you structured the problem.
The gap was concrete: the concurrency exercise needed a bounded worker pool and the submitted solution spawned unbounded goroutines, which the panel would expect to be caught at this level.
We would genuinely welcome a re-application once that area has had some time.

specimens.reading: A named exercise and a named property. This is the shape of feedback that is about the work rather than about fit — rare, and worth keeping.

non_inferences: Rejection does not mean the candidate has no engineering ability, only that the requirement bar was unmet for this specific benchmark.

mechanisms.title: Stronger Competing Candidate in Final Cohort
mechanisms.content:
# Stronger Competing Candidate in Final Cohort

Candidate cleared all passing bars, but another applicant in the same pipeline demonstrated superior domain overlap or lower onboarding overhead.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `candidate`
- **Nature:** `rule`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Causal Relations
- Masks `M-001` — Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall

### Non-Inferences
- Does not mean candidate had negative feedback; relative cohort ranking is outside candidate control.
mechanisms.summary: Candidate cleared all passing bars, but another applicant in the same pipeline demonstrated superior domain overlap or lower onboarding overhead.

specimens.label: Rejection naming the comparison

lines.text: This was a genuinely difficult decision — you cleared every bar we set.
We went with another finalist who has shipped the same payment rails we are migrating to, which shortens the ramp by a quarter or so.
If anything opens at this level again I would like to come back to you directly.

specimens.reading: Nothing here says the candidate fell short. A comparison decided it, and comparisons are not properties of either person.

non_inferences: Does not mean candidate had negative feedback; relative cohort ranking is outside candidate control.

mechanisms.title: ATS Parser Extraction Failure
mechanisms.content:
# ATS Parser Extraction Failure

Multi-column formatting, graphics, custom fonts, or unsupported document layouts cause ATS parser to corrupt or omit critical work history.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `system`
- **Nature:** `noise`
- **Removability:** `candidate`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `M-008` — Automated Keyword / Qualification Filter

### Non-Inferences
- Does not imply human recruiter evaluated and disliked candidate experience.
mechanisms.summary: Multi-column formatting, graphics, custom fonts, or unsupported document layouts cause ATS parser to corrupt or omit critical work history.

specimens.label: Parsed profile, as the ATS stored it
specimens.context: the same CV that renders correctly in a PDF reader

lines.text: Name: parsed · Email: parsed · Phone: parsed
Work experience: 0 entries
Skills: 0 entries
Raw text captured: 340 characters of a 4,100-character document
Ranking score: 12/100 — insufficient experience

specimens.reading: The document was not read and rejected; it was not read. A two-column layout and a graphic header are enough to produce this.

non_inferences: Does not imply human recruiter evaluated and disliked candidate experience.

mechanisms.title: Unstated Compensation Band Discrepancy
mechanisms.content:
# Unstated Compensation Band Discrepancy

Candidate market rate exceeds budgeted compensation for the requisition, but salary band was never published or clarified early.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `policy`
- **Nature:** `rule`
- **Removability:** `intermediary`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `M-013` — Mid-Process Role Requirement Redefinition
- Masks `M-001` — Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall

### Non-Inferences
- Rejection does not mean candidate is overpriced for the market, only mismatched with this specific employer budget.
mechanisms.summary: Candidate market rate exceeds budgeted compensation for the requisition, but salary band was never published or clarified early.

specimens.label: The number nobody published

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Before the manager round — what were your expectations again?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: 85–95k, as I mentioned at the screen.

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Right. I should be straight with you: the approved budget for this req tops out at 74k. It was never in the posting.

specimens.reading: The mismatch existed on day one and surfaced in week four. Four rounds were spent on a gap that a published band would have shown immediately.

non_inferences: Rejection does not mean candidate is overpriced for the market, only mismatched with this specific employer budget.

mechanisms.title: Pre-Selected Internal Candidate
mechanisms.content:
# Pre-Selected Internal Candidate

Requisition was publicly advertised to satisfy corporate policy or legal compliance while an internal employee was already earmarked for the role.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `policy`
- **Nature:** `incentive`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Causal Relations
- Masks `M-002` — Stronger Competing Candidate in Final Cohort

### Non-Inferences
- Cannot be asserted as fact without internal hiring log confirmation.
mechanisms.summary: Requisition was publicly advertised to satisfy corporate policy or legal compliance while an internal employee was already earmarked for the role.

specimens.label: Final round, an aside

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: How many people are you seeing for this?

lines.speaker: Hiring manager
lines.text: You are the third external. There is also someone internal who has been covering part of the scope since spring.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Understood. Is that a formal candidacy?

lines.speaker: Hiring manager
lines.text: It is. We post externally regardless — that is policy.

specimens.reading: Nothing improper is described. The posting is real, the process is real, and the odds were set before the first external application arrived.

non_inferences: Cannot be asserted as fact without internal hiring log confirmation.

mechanisms.title: Stale or Orphaned Job Requisition
mechanisms.content:
# Stale or Orphaned Job Requisition

Job posting remains active on careers page and aggregator portals despite the team having ceased active hiring or closed headcount.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `system`
- **Nature:** `void`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `M-020` — Automated Application Expiration Timeout

### Non-Inferences
- Application silence does not reflect candidate suitability.
mechanisms.summary: Job posting remains active on careers page and aggregator portals despite the team having ceased active hiring or closed headcount.

specimens.label: Asking whether the role is alive

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: I applied for this in January and again in March — is the posting current?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Let me check. That team stopped hiring in December; the listing should have come down. I will get it removed.

specimens.reading: The posting was not bait and it was not a decision. It was a record nobody owned, which is a different thing to be angry at.

non_inferences: Application silence does not reflect candidate suitability.

mechanisms.title: Headcount Freeze or Budget Cancellation
mechanisms.content:
# Headcount Freeze or Budget Cancellation

Executive leadership or finance halts all new hires across division due to macroeconomic factors or revenue shifts mid-interview process.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `policy`
- **Nature:** `rule`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `M-006` — Stale or Orphaned Job Requisition
- Masks `M-001` — Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall
- Masks `M-002` — Stronger Competing Candidate in Final Cohort

### Non-Inferences
- Candidate performance in interview was not the causal trigger for process termination.
mechanisms.summary: Executive leadership or finance halts all new hires across division due to macroeconomic factors or revenue shifts mid-interview process.

specimens.label: The freeze, as announced downward

lines.text: I have to pause our process. A hiring freeze was announced across the division this morning, effective immediately.
Your final round was scheduled for Thursday. I am cancelling it rather than having you prepare for something I cannot honour.
I will tell you plainly when I know anything, including if the answer is that this will not reopen.

specimens.reading: The cause is above the hiring loop and dated. Whether it is checkable against public news is the probe worth running.

non_inferences: Candidate performance in interview was not the causal trigger for process termination.

mechanisms.title: Automated Keyword / Qualification Filter
mechanisms.content:
# Automated Keyword / Qualification Filter

Deterministic filter rejecting applications missing exact acronyms, certifications, or specific years-of-experience thresholds.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `system`
- **Nature:** `rule`
- **Removability:** `candidate`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `M-011` — Employment Gap Downranking Bias
- Amplifies `M-013` — Mid-Process Role Requirement Redefinition — over-filtering strong generalists prolongs the search until the team redefines the role mid-process; see loop L-003

### Non-Inferences
- Passing keyword filters does not guarantee interview invitation.
mechanisms.summary: Deterministic filter rejecting applications missing exact acronyms, certifications, or specific years-of-experience thresholds.

specimens.label: Screening rules, as they ran

lines.text: Rule 1: must_contain("Kubernetes") — PASS
Rule 2: must_contain("CKA") — candidate holds CKAD — FAIL
Rule 3: not evaluated (short-circuit)
Status: Rejected — does not meet minimum criteria

specimens.reading: An adjacent certification is not a near miss to a string match; it is a miss. The filter compares tokens, not competence.

non_inferences: Passing keyword filters does not guarantee interview invitation.

mechanisms.title: Recruiter Volume & Quota Incentive Distortion
mechanisms.content:
# Recruiter Volume & Quota Incentive Distortion

Recruiters optimize for pipeline velocity and superficial pattern-matching due to overwhelming applicant volume (500+ per req).

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `recruiter`
- **Nature:** `incentive`
- **Removability:** `intermediary`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `M-012` — Interview Resource & Scheduling Saturation
- Masks `M-008` — Automated Keyword / Qualification Filter

### Non-Inferences
- Does not mean recruiter is individually negligent; reflects structural capacity mismatch.
mechanisms.summary: Recruiters optimize for pipeline velocity and superficial pattern-matching due to overwhelming applicant volume (500+ per req).

specimens.label: The queue the screen ran against

lines.text: Applications received: 640
Recruiter screening capacity this week: 40
Median time spent per profile: 7 seconds
Profiles advanced: 11

specimens.reading: Seven seconds is not a judgement of a career. It is what a queue of 640 does to attention, whoever is holding it.

non_inferences: Does not mean recruiter is individually negligent; reflects structural capacity mismatch.

mechanisms.title: Hidden Evaluation Rubric or Undisclosed Priority
mechanisms.content:
# Hidden Evaluation Rubric or Undisclosed Priority

The interview team grades candidate against specific undisclosed architectural dogmas, internal frameworks, or unwritten biases.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `hiring-manager`
- **Nature:** `bias`
- **Removability:** `intermediary`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `M-022` — Hiring Manager Consensus Impasse
- Masks `M-001` — Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall

### Non-Inferences
- Failure to guess unstated preferences is not equivalent to lack of core competence.
mechanisms.summary: The interview team grades candidate against specific undisclosed architectural dogmas, internal frameworks, or unwritten biases.

specimens.label: The rubric that was not in the brief

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: I would put a queue between them so the write path stays available if the consumer is down.

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.text: Mm. We do not use queues here.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Is that a constraint I should design within?

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.text: Just carry on.

specimens.reading: A house preference was applied as a grading criterion without being stated as one. The candidate could not have designed to a rule they were not told.

non_inferences: Failure to guess unstated preferences is not equivalent to lack of core competence.

mechanisms.title: Employment Gap Downranking Bias
mechanisms.content:
# Employment Gap Downranking Bias

Automated ranking algorithms or human screeners discount candidates with recent career breaks regardless of verified project history.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `system`
- **Nature:** `bias`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `M-008` — Automated Keyword / Qualification Filter

### Non-Inferences
- Employment gap does not correlate with underlying technical decline.
mechanisms.summary: Automated ranking algorithms or human screeners discount candidates with recent career breaks regardless of verified project history.

specimens.label: Ranking breakdown, as scored

lines.text: Skills match: 91/100
Domain match: 88/100
Continuity penalty: −22 (gap of 14 months detected)
Final rank: 57/100 — below advance threshold

specimens.reading: The penalty is applied to a date range, not to anything in the work. Nothing the candidate shipped during or after the gap is in the arithmetic.

non_inferences: Employment gap does not correlate with underlying technical decline.

mechanisms.title: Interview Resource & Scheduling Saturation
mechanisms.content:
# Interview Resource & Scheduling Saturation

Engineering interviewers are overwhelmed with sprint commitments, leading to calendar fragmentation, rush reviews, or dropped loops.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `hiring-manager`
- **Nature:** `noise`
- **Removability:** `intermediary`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `M-019` — Take-Home Evaluation Fatigue & Asymmetry

### Non-Inferences
- Rescheduling is an operational issue and does not indicate negative evaluation.
mechanisms.summary: Engineering interviewers are overwhelmed with sprint commitments, leading to calendar fragmentation, rush reviews, or dropped loops.

specimens.label: Inside the interviewer calendar

lines.speaker: Engineering manager
lines.text: Can you take the panel Thursday? Nobody else on the team is free.

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.text: I am on release duty and I have not read the take-home. I can do it but it will be a cold read.

lines.speaker: Engineering manager
lines.text: Take it. We are already two weeks over on this req.

specimens.reading: The evaluation was compromised before it began, and nothing in the candidate could have changed that. This trace lives on the other side of the table.

non_inferences: Rescheduling is an operational issue and does not indicate negative evaluation.

mechanisms.title: Mid-Process Role Requirement Redefinition
mechanisms.content:
# Mid-Process Role Requirement Redefinition

Team changes tech stack, seniority requirements, or project scope mid-funnel, invalidating previous interview assessments.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `hiring-manager`
- **Nature:** `noise`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `M-004` — Unstated Compensation Band Discrepancy
- Amplifies `M-024` — Inflated Requisition Requirements vs Actual Team Needs — each redefinition re-inflates the requisition with new must-haves instead of trimming it; see loop L-003
- Masks `M-001` — Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall

### Non-Inferences
- Candidate rejection was driven by shifting team mandate, not prior interview answers.
mechanisms.summary: Team changes tech stack, seniority requirements, or project scope mid-funnel, invalidating previous interview assessments.

specimens.label: The role that changed underneath

lines.text: Thank you for the four rounds — the panel notes were strong throughout.

Since we opened this req the team has moved the service to Rust and folded the on-call leadership into the role. Weighted against the new profile we are looking for someone with production Rust and formal lead experience.
I recognise you interviewed against the previous description. I am sorry about that.

specimens.reading: The assessments were not re-run, they were re-scored against a target that moved after they were taken.

non_inferences: Candidate rejection was driven by shifting team mandate, not prior interview answers.

mechanisms.title: Location or Timezone Compliance Constraint
mechanisms.content:
# Location or Timezone Compliance Constraint

Company legal or tax entity cannot support remote employment contracts in candidate physical residency jurisdiction.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `policy`
- **Nature:** `rule`
- **Removability:** `intermediary`

### Non-Inferences
- Legal geography barrier is completely independent of candidate technical competence.
mechanisms.summary: Company legal or tax entity cannot support remote employment contracts in candidate physical residency jurisdiction.

specimens.label: Where the constraint actually sits

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Everything is agreed on our side. One question — you are resident where exactly?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Same country as in my application, no change.

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Then I have bad news. We have no legal entity there and our provider does not cover it, so we cannot issue a contract regardless of the role.

specimens.reading: A hard constraint that is knowable on day one and was checked at the offer. Nothing about the candidate is being assessed here.

non_inferences: Legal geography barrier is completely independent of candidate technical competence.

mechanisms.title: Communication or Working Style Friction
mechanisms.content:
# Communication or Working Style Friction

Candidate demonstrated abrasive tone, defensive reactions to critique, or inability to listen during collaborative interview problem solving.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `candidate`
- **Nature:** `bias`
- **Removability:** `candidate`

### Non-Inferences
- Style friction during high-stress interview is not a permanent personality defect.
mechanisms.summary: Candidate demonstrated abrasive tone, defensive reactions to critique, or inability to listen during collaborative interview problem solving.

specimens.label: The exchange the note refers to

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.text: I think this loop is doing more work than it needs to.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: It is fine. The input is bounded.

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.text: Sure, but if it were not?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Then I would change it. But it is.

specimens.reading: The panel recorded this as resistance to critique. A short answer under time pressure and a defensive posture look identical in a transcript — which is why this belongs in the honest-baseline set and not in the excuses.

non_inferences: Style friction during high-stress interview is not a permanent personality defect.

mechanisms.title: Speculative Sourcing / Talent Pooling Without Opening
mechanisms.content:
# Speculative Sourcing / Talent Pooling Without Opening

Recruiters proactively gather candidate pools for future anticipated headcount that is not yet authorized or funded.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `recruiter`
- **Nature:** `incentive`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `M-009` — Recruiter Volume & Quota Incentive Distortion

### Non-Inferences
- Ghosting after outbound message indicates absence of immediate opening, not profile rejection.
mechanisms.summary: Recruiters proactively gather candidate pools for future anticipated headcount that is not yet authorized or funded.

specimens.label: What the outreach was actually for

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Great talking today. To set expectations — is there an open requisition behind this?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Not yet. We are building a bench ahead of the Q3 planning round; if the headcount is approved you would be first in line.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Understood, thanks for saying so.

specimens.reading: A straight answer converts a mystery into a schedule. The same silence three months later means something entirely different once this line exists.

non_inferences: Ghosting after outbound message indicates absence of immediate opening, not profile rejection.

mechanisms.title: Experience-Age Grading Mismatch
mechanisms.content:
# Experience-Age Grading Mismatch

Candidate with 10+ years applied for mid/senior role, triggering fears of boredom, rapid churn, or salary dissatisfaction.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `recruiter`
- **Nature:** `bias`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `M-004` — Unstated Compensation Band Discrepancy
- Masks `M-001` — Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall

### Non-Inferences
- Being rejected as "overqualified" is an organizational tier mismatch, not a candidate deficiency.
mechanisms.summary: Candidate with 10+ years applied for mid/senior role, triggering fears of boredom, rapid churn, or salary dissatisfaction.

specimens.label: Screening note, internal

lines.text: 12 years experience against a role scoped at 4–6.
Concern: likely to be bored within two quarters; salary expectation probably above band; risk of using us as a bridge.
Recommend: pass, unless the manager wants to see them for the level above.

specimens.reading: Every line is a forecast about the future, none is an observation about the work. This is why the rejection can arrive before any technical signal exists.

non_inferences: Being rejected as "overqualified" is an organizational tier mismatch, not a candidate deficiency.

mechanisms.title: Domain Specificity Over-Weighting
mechanisms.content:
# Domain Specificity Over-Weighting

Interviewer requires exact vertical experience (e.g. adtech, crypto, specific payment processor) over deep transferable systems fundamentals.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `hiring-manager`
- **Nature:** `bias`
- **Removability:** `intermediary`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `M-010` — Hidden Evaluation Rubric or Undisclosed Priority
- Masks `M-001` — Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall

### Non-Inferences
- Transferable general engineering skills are not disproven by lack of specific proprietary protocol knowledge.
mechanisms.summary: Interviewer requires exact vertical experience (e.g. adtech, crypto, specific payment processor) over deep transferable systems fundamentals.

specimens.label: Where the round turned

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.text: You have built settlement systems, but not in cards specifically?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Not cards. Same problem shape though — idempotency, reconciliation, chargeback-equivalent reversals.

lines.speaker: Interviewer
lines.text: We really need someone who has lived in card rails. The scheme rules are their own world.

specimens.reading: Transferable depth was heard and set aside for vertical familiarity. That is a legitimate preference and a narrow one; the rejection is about the filter, not the engineering.

non_inferences: Transferable general engineering skills are not disproven by lack of specific proprietary protocol knowledge.

mechanisms.title: Take-Home Evaluation Fatigue & Asymmetry
mechanisms.content:
# Take-Home Evaluation Fatigue & Asymmetry

Reviewers perform hurried 5-minute scans of complex 15-hour take-home projects, missing subtle architectural patterns and tests.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `hiring-manager`
- **Nature:** `noise`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `M-012` — Interview Resource & Scheduling Saturation
- Masks `M-001` — Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall

### Non-Inferences
- Take-home rejection under evaluation fatigue does not measure true software engineering craftsmanship.
mechanisms.summary: Reviewers perform hurried 5-minute scans of complex 15-hour take-home projects, missing subtle architectural patterns and tests.

specimens.label: Review record for a 15-hour submission

lines.text: Submission: 41 files, 78 tests, migrations, README with design rationale.
Reviewer time logged: 6 minutes. Files opened: 3.
Note: no tests visible, structure unclear.

specimens.reading: The note is false about the submission and true about the review. The asymmetry between the two efforts is the mechanism.

non_inferences: Take-home rejection under evaluation fatigue does not measure true software engineering craftsmanship.

mechanisms.title: Automated Application Expiration Timeout
mechanisms.content:
# Automated Application Expiration Timeout

ATS configuration automatically issues bulk rejections to all pending unreviewed applications after 45 or 60 days.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `system`
- **Nature:** `rule`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Causal Relations
- Masks `M-006` — Stale or Orphaned Job Requisition

### Non-Inferences
- Bulk timeout rejection contains zero qualitative assessment of candidate profile.
mechanisms.summary: ATS configuration automatically issues bulk rejections to all pending unreviewed applications after 45 or 60 days.

specimens.label: Bulk expiry, as logged

lines.text: Scheduled job: expire_stale_applications
Selecting applications with status=submitted and age>60d — 312 matched
Human review recorded on 0 of 312
Status set to Rejected — 312 notification emails queued

specimens.reading: The rejection email is real and the review it implies never happened. Timing is the tell: everyone in the batch is notified in the same minute.

non_inferences: Bulk timeout rejection contains zero qualitative assessment of candidate profile.

mechanisms.title: Reference Check Discrepancy or Regulatory Ineligibility
mechanisms.content:
# Reference Check Discrepancy or Regulatory Ineligibility

Third-party check reveals unverified employment dates, unconfirmed degrees, or direct conflict of interest.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `candidate`
- **Nature:** `rule`
- **Removability:** `candidate`

### Non-Inferences
- Administrative mismatch in dates is distinct from fraudulent resume misrepresentation.
mechanisms.summary: Third-party check reveals unverified employment dates, unconfirmed degrees, or direct conflict of interest.

specimens.label: Where the check disagreed with the record

lines.text: The background provider returned a mismatch on employment dates for one role: our vendor has March 2019 – June 2021, your application states January 2019 – August 2021.
We are required to pause the offer while this is reconciled. If you have a payslip or contract covering those months, that resolves it.

specimens.reading: A resolvable discrepancy in a third-party record, with a named document that closes it. This is one of the few mechanisms with a direct, evidenced remedy.

non_inferences: Administrative mismatch in dates is distinct from fraudulent resume misrepresentation.

mechanisms.title: Hiring Manager Consensus Impasse
mechanisms.content:
# Hiring Manager Consensus Impasse

The interview panel splits 50/50 without an executive tiebreaker, defaulting conservatively to a "no-hire" decision.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `hiring-manager`
- **Nature:** `bias`
- **Removability:** `none`

### Causal Relations
- Masks `M-002` — Stronger Competing Candidate in Final Cohort

### Non-Inferences
- Split panel reflects lack of calibrated internal standards rather than candidate failure.
mechanisms.summary: The interview panel splits 50/50 without an executive tiebreaker, defaulting conservatively to a "no-hire" decision.

specimens.label: Debrief tally

lines.text: Interviewer A: hire. Interviewer B: hire. Interviewer C: no hire. Interviewer D: no hire.
No tiebreaker present. Policy: absent consensus, default to no hire.
Outcome recorded as: not aligned with team needs.

specimens.reading: A 2–2 split became a rejection by rule, and the rule was then written up as a judgement about the candidate.

non_inferences: Split panel reflects lack of calibrated internal standards rather than candidate failure.

mechanisms.title: Portfolio / Work Artifact Misinterpretation
mechanisms.content:
# Portfolio / Work Artifact Misinterpretation

Screeners overlook candidate role architecture due to non-standard repository layout or unindexed open-source contributions.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `candidate`
- **Nature:** `noise`
- **Removability:** `candidate`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `M-001` — Genuine Technical Skill Shortfall

### Non-Inferences
- Misinterpreted architecture can be corrected through structured documentation.
mechanisms.summary: Screeners overlook candidate role architecture due to non-standard repository layout or unindexed open-source contributions.

specimens.label: What the screener saw and what was there

lines.text: Screener note: mostly forks, little original work, no evidence of architecture ownership.
The account: 3 pinned forks, and 40 commits over two years to an upstream project under a different org — including the storage layer rewrite referenced in the CV.

specimens.reading: The work exists and the surface that was checked does not show it. This is a discovery failure, and it is one of the few the candidate can fix directly.

non_inferences: Misinterpreted architecture can be corrected through structured documentation.

mechanisms.title: Inflated Requisition Requirements vs Actual Team Needs
mechanisms.content:
# Inflated Requisition Requirements vs Actual Team Needs

Job description demands 10+ niche technologies and Staff-level qualifications for a straightforward feature engineering role.

### Structural Context
- **Actor:** `hiring-manager`
- **Nature:** `incentive`
- **Removability:** `intermediary`

### Causal Relations
- Amplifies `M-008` — Automated Keyword / Qualification Filter
- Amplifies `M-004` — Unstated Compensation Band Discrepancy

### Non-Inferences
- Failing to meet an inflated "wishlist" does not mean candidate cannot excel at the team’s actual core tasks.
mechanisms.summary: Job description demands 10+ niche technologies and Staff-level qualifications for a straightforward feature engineering role.

specimens.label: The posting against the first month of work

lines.text: Posting: 10+ years distributed systems, Kubernetes, Kafka, Rust, Go, Terraform, GraphQL, ML serving, on-call leadership, mentoring.
Same team, standup notes from the quarter: CRUD endpoints for the billing dashboard, a report export, two library upgrades.
Both descriptions are of the same role.

specimens.reading: The requirement list is a wish, an anchor and a filter at once. It describes the ceiling somebody imagined, not the work in the sprint.

non_inferences: Failing to meet an inflated "wishlist" does not mean candidate cannot excel at the team’s actual core tasks.

patterns.title: Seniority Double Bind
patterns.content:
# Seniority Double Bind

Candidate is simultaneously rejected as overqualified for junior/mid roles and underqualified (or insufficiently specialized) for staff/leadership roles.

### Trigger Rule
Candidate observes rejection for overqualification at level N and skill-depth shortfall at level N+1 within the same market cycle.

### What this Establishes
- Candidate falls into an evaluation boundary gap where compensation/experience expectations mismatch standard job tiers.

### What this Does NOT Establish
- Does not establish that the candidate lacks market value.
- Does not establish malice or coordinated collusion between employers.
patterns.summary: Candidate is simultaneously rejected as overqualified for junior/mid roles and underqualified (or insufficiently specialized) for staff/leadership roles.
patterns.trigger_rule: Candidate observes rejection for overqualification at level N and skill-depth shortfall at level N+1 within the same market cycle.
establishes: Candidate falls into an evaluation boundary gap where compensation/experience expectations mismatch standard job tiers.
non_inferences: Does not establish that the candidate lacks market value.
Does not establish malice or coordinated collusion between employers.

specimens.label: Two rejections, six weeks apart
specimens.context: same candidate, same market, adjacent levels

lines.text: 12 Feb — Senior Backend Engineer (level 4). Your experience sits above the band scoped for this role and we were concerned it would not hold your interest.
26 Mar — Staff Engineer (level 5). The panel felt the depth of platform ownership was not yet at staff scope; we would look for a broader track record of org-wide impact.
Both roles: same city, same domain, same six-week window.

specimens.reading: Neither message is unreasonable on its own. Put next to each other they describe a candidate who is above one level and below the next, with nothing in between open.

specimens.label: What the pair does and does not establish

lines.text: Established: two rejections, two stated grounds, two adjacent levels, one market cycle.

Not established: that either judgement was wrong, that the two employers coordinated, or that the candidate is unhireable. The motif is a property of the level grid, not of the person moving through it.

specimens.reading: The pattern is worth naming precisely because each half is defensible. The trap is structural, which is also why no single conversation can argue it away.

patterns.title: Closed-Then-Reposted Requisition Motif
patterns.content:
# Closed-Then-Reposted Requisition Motif

A candidate completes multiple late-stage interviews, is rejected with a generic message, and sees the identical role reposted weeks later.

### Trigger Rule
Candidate observes role closure/rejection followed by public reopening of materially similar role listing within 60 days.

### What this Establishes
- The requisition requirements or target profile were not satisfied by the interviewed pool, or search criteria changed mid-process.

### What this Does NOT Establish
- Does not establish that the original job listing was fake or a ghost job.
- Does not establish that candidate was intentionally misled.
patterns.summary: A candidate completes multiple late-stage interviews, is rejected with a generic message, and sees the identical role reposted weeks later.
patterns.trigger_rule: Candidate observes role closure/rejection followed by public reopening of materially similar role listing within 60 days.
establishes: The requisition requirements or target profile were not satisfied by the interviewed pool, or search criteria changed mid-process.
non_inferences: Does not establish that the original job listing was fake or a ghost job.
Does not establish that candidate was intentionally misled.

specimens.label: The sequence, as recorded

lines.text: Applied — req #4471
Recruiter screen — passed
Technical panel — passed
Final round with hiring manager — completed
Rejected — generic template, no specifics given
req #4471 visible on the careers page again, text unchanged

specimens.reading: Late-stage progress, a contentless rejection, and the same requisition number back on the board. The sequence is the observation; its cause is not in the sequence.

specimens.label: The question that splits the branches

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: I saw req #4471 listed again. Is this a new opening on the team, or the same one?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Same requisition. We restarted the search with a revised profile after the first round of interviews.

specimens.reading: A revised profile, an automated refresh and a genuinely new headcount are three different mechanisms with one appearance. This is the question that tells them apart.

patterns.title: Experience-Age Impossibility
patterns.content:
# Experience-Age Impossibility

Requisition requires more years of hands-on experience in a specific framework or tool than that technology has existed in the open-source ecosystem.

### Trigger Rule
Job description or automated screen requires X years of experience where X > technology_age.

### What this Establishes
- Job description was authored without technical review, using copy-paste templates with automated gating rules.

### What this Does NOT Establish
- Does not imply technical team is incompetent, only that HR screening pipeline lacks technical validation.
patterns.summary: Requisition requires more years of hands-on experience in a specific framework or tool than that technology has existed in the open-source ecosystem.
patterns.trigger_rule: Job description or automated screen requires X years of experience where X > technology_age.
establishes: Job description was authored without technical review, using copy-paste templates with automated gating rules.
non_inferences: Does not imply technical team is incompetent, only that HR screening pipeline lacks technical validation.

specimens.label: The requirement, as published
specimens.subject: Senior Platform Engineer — requirements

lines.text: 7+ years of production experience with Kubernetes.
5+ years with a framework first released three years ago.
Screening is automated: applications below the stated year counts are filtered before human review.

specimens.reading: This is checkable against a release date, which makes it one of the few claims in hiring that can simply be false rather than debatable.

specimens.label: What the filter did with it

lines.text: Application submitted
Rule: years_with_framework >= 5 — candidate value 3 — FAIL
Status: Rejected — does not meet minimum criteria

specimens.reading: No one decided anything about this candidate. An impossible threshold was copied into a rule and the rule ran.

patterns.title: Compensation Double Bind
patterns.content:
# Compensation Double Bind

Candidate is required to state salary expectation first; quoting high triggers immediate rejection, while quoting low triggers leveling downranking.

### Trigger Rule
Asymmetric salary inquiry where employer refuses band disclosure prior to candidate submitting binding number.

### What this Establishes
- Information asymmetry is utilized as an uncalibrated gatekeeper before technical merit is evaluated.

### What this Does NOT Establish
- Does not mean employer has unlimited budget or malice.
patterns.summary: Candidate is required to state salary expectation first; quoting high triggers immediate rejection, while quoting low triggers leveling downranking.
patterns.trigger_rule: Asymmetric salary inquiry where employer refuses band disclosure prior to candidate submitting binding number.
establishes: Information asymmetry is utilized as an uncalibrated gatekeeper before technical merit is evaluated.
non_inferences: Does not mean employer has unlimited budget or malice.

specimens.label: The asymmetry, in four messages

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Before we go further — what are your compensation expectations?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Happy to discuss. What is the band for the role?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: We prefer to hear the candidate number first so we can match it to the right level.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Understood. My expectation is in the range of 85–95k.

specimens.reading: The number is required from one side and withheld by the other, and it is collected before the level is fixed. Both outcomes below follow from that ordering.

specimens.label: The two branches
specimens.context: the same question, two candidates, one week

lines.text: Quoted 95k — We are not able to proceed; the expectation is outside the range we have for this role.
Quoted 70k — Good news, we would like to move ahead. Based on the conversation we are looking at this as a mid-level hire rather than senior.

specimens.reading: A high number ends the process and a low one moves the level. There is no answer that leaves both the process and the grade untouched — which is what makes it a bind rather than a negotiation.

loops.title: Employment Gap Penalty Loop
loops.content:
# Employment Gap Penalty Loop

An employment gap triggers automated downranking (M-011), which pushes the profile below keyword and qualification filters (M-008); fewer interview invitations lengthen the gap, which in turn strengthens the downranking.

### Cycle Dynamics
This causal loop reinforces mechanisms across iterations:
- `M-011` amplifies `M-008`
- `M-008` amplifies `M-011`
loops.summary: An employment gap triggers automated downranking (M-011), which pushes the profile below keyword and qualification filters (M-008); fewer interview invitations lengthen the gap, which in turn strengthens the downranking.

specimens.label: The same profile, two cycles apart
specimens.context: same CV, same market, nine months between

lines.text: Cycle 1 — skills 91, domain 88, continuity penalty −22 (gap 14 months) → rank 57
Cycle 2 — skills 91, domain 88, continuity penalty −34 (gap 23 months) → rank 45
Advance threshold both times: 60.

specimens.reading: Nothing in the work changed between the two rows. The only variable that moved is the one the penalty reads, and it moves because the penalty worked the first time.

specimens.label: Why the loop closes

lines.text: Downranking pushes the profile below the filter threshold.
Below the threshold there are no interviews.
No interviews means no offer, so the gap continues to grow.
A longer gap increases the penalty on the next application.

specimens.reading: Each step is a reasonable rule on its own. Together they form a cycle whose input is its own output.

loops.title: Take-Home Opportunity-Cost Saturation Loop
loops.content:
# Take-Home Opportunity-Cost Saturation Loop

Candidates invest heavy hours into unbounded take-home assignments, reducing bandwidth for applications, while reviewers suffer evaluation fatigue.

### Cycle Dynamics
This causal loop reinforces mechanisms across iterations:
- `M-012` amplifies `M-019`
- `M-019` amplifies `M-012`
loops.summary: Candidates invest heavy hours into unbounded take-home assignments, reducing bandwidth for applications, while reviewers suffer evaluation fatigue.

specimens.label: One month of a candidate calendar

lines.text: Take-home A: 14 hours. Take-home B: 11 hours. Take-home C: 16 hours.
Applications sent that month: 4 — down from 21 the month before.
Outcomes: two rejections after sub-ten-minute reviews, one no response, one still open.

specimens.reading: The hours are real and they come out of the same budget as the search itself. Fewer applications is not a change in motivation; it is arithmetic.

specimens.label: The same month from the reviewer side

lines.text: Submissions in the queue: 19 · Reviewer capacity: 2 hours per week
Median review time per submission: 6 minutes.
Reviewers report the assignments are too large to assess properly, and the scope is set by the same team.

specimens.reading: Both sides are short of the same thing. Larger assignments do not buy better signal — they buy shallower reads, which is what makes it a loop rather than a trade-off.

loops.title: Inflated-Requirements Search Saturation Loop
loops.content:
# Inflated-Requirements Search Saturation Loop

Teams write inflated requirements, filtering out strong generalists, prolonging open search, causing recruiter fatigue and mid-process role redefinitions.

### Cycle Dynamics
This causal loop reinforces mechanisms across iterations:
- `M-024` amplifies `M-008`
- `M-008` amplifies `M-013`
- `M-013` amplifies `M-024`
loops.summary: Teams write inflated requirements, filtering out strong generalists, prolonging open search, causing recruiter fatigue and mid-process role redefinitions.

specimens.label: The same requisition, rewritten twice

lines.text: Month 0 — 8 required technologies, 7+ years, staff-level scope. Applications: 340. Advanced to onsite: 2. Hired: 0.
Month 3 — search still open. Requirements rewritten upward: 10 technologies, 9+ years, plus formal lead experience.
Month 6 — search still open. Recruiter reassigned; team now covering the work with overtime.

specimens.reading: The response to a failed search was a narrower filter. The filter was the reason the search failed, which is the turn that makes this a loop.

specimens.label: Where the requirement came from

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Do we really need nine years and Rust for this? The backlog is mostly billing endpoints.

lines.speaker: Hiring manager
lines.text: Nobody good has applied in three months. If we lower the bar we will get more of the same.

specimens.reading: The inference runs backwards: an empty pipeline is read as evidence that the bar is too low. That reading is what tightens the next iteration.

interventions.title: Auto-Close Stale Job Requisitions
interventions.content:
# Auto-Close Stale Job Requisitions

Implement automated ATS policy to expire public listings when headcount authorization lapses or no interview activity occurs within 60 days.

### Expected Effects
- Reduce stale public listings and candidate application waste
- Reduce ambiguous post-application silence

### Measurements
- `stale_requisition_rate`
- `closure_latency_days`
interventions.summary: Implement automated ATS policy to expire public listings when headcount authorization lapses or no interview activity occurs within 60 days.
expected_effects: Reduce stale public listings and candidate application waste

specimens.label: The rule, and what it did

lines.text: Policy: expire_listing when headcount_authorisation lapses OR no interview activity for 45 days
req #4471 — last interview activity 47 days ago → listing withdrawn from careers page and aggregators
Candidates with applications in flight: 84 — each notified that the search has closed, with the date.

specimens.reading: The same batch job that produces silent bulk rejections can be pointed at the listing instead of the candidate. The cost is a configuration line.

interventions.title: Upfront Compensation Band Disclosure
interventions.content:
# Upfront Compensation Band Disclosure

Publish verified salary and equity bands directly in job descriptions or disclose them prior to scheduling technical interview rounds.

### Expected Effects
- Eliminate late-stage compensation mismatch dropouts
- Reduce time wasted on mismatched leveling conversations

### Measurements
- `late_stage_compensation_drop_rate`
- `candidate_pipeline_satisfaction`
interventions.summary: Publish verified salary and equity bands directly in job descriptions or disclose them prior to scheduling technical interview rounds.
expected_effects: Reduce time wasted on mismatched leveling conversations

specimens.label: The posting with the band in it
specimens.subject: Senior Backend Engineer · Payments

lines.text: Level: L4 · Base band: 68,000–79,000 · Equity: 0.02–0.04% · Band verified by finance on 3 March.
We will not ask for your expectations before showing you this number.
If your expectation sits above the band, tell us at the screen and we will say honestly whether the level can move.

specimens.reading: Every branch of the compensation bind needs the candidate to speak first. Publishing the number removes the asymmetry the bind is built on.

interventions.title: Standardized Late-Stage Rejection Feedback Taxonomy
interventions.content:
# Standardized Late-Stage Rejection Feedback Taxonomy

Provide candidates reaching technical or panel stages with structured, rubric-based feedback categories rather than generic templates.

### Expected Effects
- Provide actionable feedback signals to candidates
- Enforce consistent interviewer calibration across rounds

### Measurements
- `informative_feedback_ratio`
- `interviewer_calibration_variance`
interventions.summary: Provide candidates reaching technical or panel stages with structured, rubric-based feedback categories rather than generic templates.
expected_effects: Provide actionable feedback signals to candidates
Enforce consistent interviewer calibration across rounds

specimens.label: The rejection, rewritten to the taxonomy
specimens.subject: Outcome — technical panel

lines.text: Category: technical depth · Sub-category: complexity reasoning · Round: technical panel, exercise 2
What we saw: a correct quadratic solution where the panel was looking for the linear approach, reached without prompting.
What we did not assess: system design, collaboration, or domain knowledge — those rounds were positive or not reached.
Re-application window: six months, straight to the technical panel.

specimens.reading: The same decision, expressed as a category with a scope. Note the second line: saying what was not assessed is what stops a single round becoming a verdict on the person.

interventions.title: Remove Career Gap Feature from Automated Ranking Models
interventions.content:
# Remove Career Gap Feature from Automated Ranking Models

Disable employment duration gap penalties in recruitment AI algorithms and screening models.

### Expected Effects
- Break algorithmic unemployment penalty loop
- Broaden candidate pool to include skilled returning talent

### Measurements
- `gap_candidate_screen_rate`
- `long_term_placement_success`
interventions.summary: Disable employment duration gap penalties in recruitment AI algorithms and screening models.
expected_effects: Broaden candidate pool to include skilled returning talent

specimens.label: The same profile, with the feature removed

lines.text: Skills match: 91/100 · Domain match: 88/100
Continuity penalty: feature disabled
Final rank: 89/100 — advanced to recruiter queue
Model card updated: employment_gap removed from feature set, 14 March.

specimens.reading: The arithmetic is the whole intervention. The same person, the same work, above the threshold instead of below it.

interventions.title: Candidate ATS Parser Conformance Test Utility
interventions.content:
# Candidate ATS Parser Conformance Test Utility

Provide candidates with an open-source parsing validation tool to verify CV machine-readability before submission.

### Expected Effects
- Eliminate formatting-induced silent parsing failures
- Increase candidate confidence in resume ingestion fidelity

### Measurements
- `parser_extraction_error_rate`
- `ingestion_pass_rate`
interventions.summary: Provide candidates with an open-source parsing validation tool to verify CV machine-readability before submission.
expected_effects: Increase candidate confidence in resume ingestion fidelity

interventions.title: Strict Take-Home Timebox & Blinded Evaluation Rubric
interventions.content:
# Strict Take-Home Timebox & Blinded Evaluation Rubric

Enforce strict 3-hour scope limits on take-homes, compensate candidates for extended samples, and grade submissions blind.

### Expected Effects
- Prevent reviewer fatigue and asymmetric code evaluation
- Respect candidate time investment and eliminate IP exploitation concerns

### Measurements
- `take_home_completion_rate`
- `inter_rater_rubric_correlation`
interventions.summary: Enforce strict 3-hour scope limits on take-homes, compensate candidates for extended samples, and grade submissions blind.
expected_effects: Prevent reviewer fatigue and asymmetric code evaluation
Respect candidate time investment and eliminate IP exploitation concerns

specimens.label: The brief and the review record, both bounded
specimens.subject: Take-home — Senior Backend Engineer

lines.text: Scope: one endpoint with persistence and tests. Hard timebox: 3 hours. Submit whatever you have at the three-hour mark.
Anything beyond three hours is paid at our contractor rate; tell us in advance if you want that option.
Review: submissions are anonymised before grading and scored against the published rubric by two reviewers, minimum 20 minutes each.

specimens.reading: Both halves of the asymmetry are addressed at once: the candidate hours are capped and the reviewer minutes have a floor. Capping only one side moves the problem rather than closing it.

evidence.title: Hidden Workers: Untapped Talent (HBS / Accenture)
evidence.summary: Survey of 8,000 workers and 2,250 executives in the US, UK and Germany on automated hiring. 88% of employers agree that qualified high-skill candidates are vetted out of the process by applicant tracking systems because they do not match the exact criteria of the job description; the report attributes a large "hidden worker" population to configurable ATS exclusion rules and knock-out filters.
evidence.citation: Fuller, J. B., Raman, M., Sage-Gavin, E., & Hines, K. (2021). Hidden Workers: Untapped Talent. Harvard Business School Project on Managing the Future of Work & Accenture.

evidence.title: Too Good to Hire? Capability and Inferences about Commitment in Labor Markets
evidence.summary: Four experiments with hiring managers show that candidates signalling more capability than the role requires are perceived as less committed to the organization and are penalized in hiring decisions — direct evidence for "overqualified" rejections and the seniority double bind.
evidence.citation: Galperin, R. V., Hahl, O., Sterling, A. D., & Guo, J. (2020). Administrative Science Quarterly, 65(2), 275–313.

evidence.title: Duration Dependence and Labor Market Conditions: Evidence from a Field Experiment
evidence.summary: Field experiment sending roughly 12,000 fictitious résumés to about 3,000 postings in 100 US cities: the probability of an interview callback falls sharply with the length of the current unemployment spell (most of the decline within the first eight months) and the penalty is stronger in tighter labor markets — employers use gap length as a screening signal.
evidence.citation: Kroft, K., Lange, F., & Notowidigdo, M. J. (2013). The Quarterly Journal of Economics, 128(3), 1123–1167.

evidence.title: Job Seekers Beware of Ghost Jobs (Clarify Capital survey of hiring managers)
evidence.summary: Survey of 1,045 managers involved in hiring (fielded 31 Aug – 1 Sep 2022) on job postings kept live without active hiring: about half keep postings open because they are "always open to new people", 43% cite giving the impression that the company is growing or keeping existing employees motivated, one in three postings had been active for more than 30 days, and one in four respondents did not plan to fill the role for three months or longer.
evidence.citation: Clarify Capital (2022). Job Seekers Beware of Ghost Jobs. Survey of 1,045 hiring managers, 31 Aug – 1 Sep 2022.

evidence.title: Salary Transparency: Growth Slows, but Momentum Continues (Indeed Hiring Lab)
evidence.summary: Tracks the share of US job postings on Indeed that disclose pay: 57.8% in September 2024, up from 52.2% a year earlier, with wide variation by occupation. Roughly four in ten postings still omit compensation — the structural precondition for compensation-band discrepancies surfacing only at late stages.
evidence.citation: Indeed Hiring Lab (2024, October 23). Salary Transparency: Growth Slows, but Momentum Continues.

evidence.title: Employment Interview Reliability: New Meta-Analytic Estimates by Structure and Format
evidence.summary: Meta-analysis of 125 inter-rater reliability coefficients (N = 32,428): reliability is substantially higher for panel interviews than for separate interviews by different interviewers (.74 vs .44) and rises with interview structure — quantifying how much interviewer variance, rather than candidate performance, drives divergent verdicts.
evidence.citation: Huffcutt, A. I., Culbertson, S. S., & Weyhrauch, W. S. (2013). International Journal of Selection and Assessment, 21(3), 264–276.

evidence.title: Federal funds target range and effective rate (FRED)
evidence.summary: The FOMC held the federal funds target range at 0.00–0.25% from 16 December 2008 to 15 December 2015 and again from 16 March 2020 to 16 March 2022. In every full month inside those two windows the effective federal funds rate stayed between 0.05% and 0.22%. Verified against the full daily DFEDTARU/DFEDTARL series (2,556 and 731 daily observations respectively, no other value in either window) and the monthly FEDFUNDS series.
evidence.citation: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (US), Federal Funds Target Range — Upper Limit [DFEDTARU], Lower Limit [DFEDTARL] and Federal Funds Effective Rate [FEDFUNDS], retrieved from FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, 27 August 2026.

evidence.title: ECB deposit facility rate (FRED)
evidence.summary: The ECB deposit facility rate was cut to 0.00% on 11 July 2012, turned negative at −0.10% on 11 June 2014, reached −0.50% on 18 September 2019 and returned to 0.00% on 27 July 2022. Every one of the 3,668 daily observations between 11 July 2012 and 26 July 2022 is at or below zero.
evidence.citation: European Central Bank, ECB Deposit Facility Rate for Euro Area [ECBDFR], retrieved from FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, 27 August 2026.

evidence.title: PitchBook-NVCA Venture Monitor, Q4 2021
evidence.summary: US venture-backed companies raised $329.6 billion in 2021, against a previous record of $166.6 billion in 2020. The report states the figures verbatim; they are data-provider estimates and are revised in later vintages.
evidence.citation: PitchBook Data and National Venture Capital Association, Q4 2021 PitchBook-NVCA Venture Monitor, 13 January 2022.

evidence.title: KPMG Venture Pulse, Q4 2021
evidence.summary: Global venture capital investment totalled $671 billion across 2021, the highest annual figure in the series, of which $171.4 billion was invested in Q4 2021 across 8,710 deals. Underlying data provided by PitchBook as of 31 December 2021.
evidence.citation: KPMG Private Enterprise, Venture Pulse Q4 2021: Global analysis of venture funding, 19 January 2022, p. 7.

evidence.title: Technology IPO profitability, 1980–2025 (Ritter)
evidence.summary: Of 121 US technology listings in 2021, 21% were profitable on trailing- twelve-month earnings. The profitable share ranged from 15% to 43% in every year from 2011 to 2021, so a listing route remained open to companies without trailing profits throughout the period.
evidence.citation: Ritter, Jay R. (2026). Initial Public Offerings: Technology Stock IPOs, Table 4b — Technology and Life Science Company IPOs, 1980–2025. University of Florida.

evidence.title: 26 U.S.C. §174 as it stood before 2022
evidence.summary: Under section 174(a)(1) as it stood before the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act took effect, a taxpayer could treat research or experimental expenditures paid or incurred in connection with a trade or business as expenses not chargeable to capital account, deductible in the year paid or incurred. Payroll spent on building product reduced taxable income in the same year it was spent.
evidence.citation: 26 U.S.C. §174, United States Code, 2017 Edition. U.S. Government Publishing Office.

evidence.title: 26 U.S.C. §174 after the 2017 amendment
evidence.summary: Section 13206(a) of Public Law 115-97 rewrote section 174 to deny any current deduction for specified research or experimental expenditures and to require them to be charged to capital account and amortised ratably over five years beginning with the midpoint of the taxable year in which they are paid or incurred, effective for amounts paid or incurred in tax years beginning after 31 December 2021. Subsection (c)(3) treats any amount paid or incurred in connection with the development of software as such an expenditure, so roughly 10% of a developer's salary was deductible in the year it was paid.
evidence.citation: 26 U.S.C. §174, United States Code, 2023 Edition. U.S. Government Publishing Office. Amendment: Pub. L. 115-97 §13206(a).

evidence.title: Rev. Proc. 2025-28 (IRS)
evidence.summary: IRS guidance on the 2025 restoration: foreign research or experimental expenditures keep the 15-year amortisation period; balances capitalised under the 2022–2024 rules may be recovered in full in the first tax year beginning after 31 December 2024 or ratably over two years; and a taxpayer meeting the section 448(c) gross-receipts test — $31,000,000 average annual gross receipts over the three prior tax years for a year beginning in 2025 — may elect the new treatment retroactively to tax years beginning after 31 December 2021, by 6 July 2026.
evidence.citation: Internal Revenue Service, Rev. Proc. 2025-28, Internal Revenue Bulletin 2025-38, sections 2.02, 2.03(1), 2.06 and 3.02(1).

evidence.title: 26 U.S.C. §174A — domestic research expenditures
evidence.summary: Section 70302(a) of Public Law 119-21, enacted 4 July 2025, added section 174A, which allows a deduction for domestic research or experimental expenditures paid or incurred during the taxable year notwithstanding section 263, with an election to capitalise and amortise them over not less than 60 months instead. Effective for amounts paid or incurred in tax years beginning after 31 December 2024.
evidence.citation: 26 U.S.C. §174A, Domestic research or experimental expenditures. Added by Pub. L. 119-21 §70302(a), 4 July 2025.

evidence.title: FOMC policy rate decisions (Open Market Operations)
evidence.summary: The FOMC raised the federal funds target range to 5.25–5.50% effective 27 July 2023, the peak of the tightening cycle, and held it there until the 25 basis point reduction of 18 September 2024 — roughly fourteen months.
evidence.citation: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (US), Open Market Operations, policy tools archive.

evidence.title: NASDAQ Composite Index (FRED)
evidence.summary: The NASDAQ Composite fell 36.4% from its record close of 16,057.44 on 19 November 2021 to its cycle low close of 10,213.29 on 28 December 2022.
evidence.citation: NASDAQ OMX Group, NASDAQ Composite Index [NASDAQCOM], retrieved from FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, 27 August 2026.

evidence.title: PitchBook-NVCA Venture Monitor, Q4 2023
evidence.summary: Every stage of the US private funding chain contracted at once. Deal value fell from $348.0 billion in 2021 to $170.6 billion in 2023. Exit value reached a decade low of $61.5 billion across an estimated 1,129 events. New fund commitments fell to a six-year low of $66.9 billion across 474 funds, against $169.2 billion in 2021 and $172.8 billion in 2022.
evidence.citation: PitchBook Data and National Venture Capital Association, Q4 2023 PitchBook-NVCA Venture Monitor, January 2024.

evidence.title: US information-sector employment (BLS CES)
evidence.summary: US payroll employment in the information sector (NAICS 51 — software publishing, data processing and telecommunications, but not computer systems design) fell from a November 2022 peak of 3,115,000 to 2,780,000 in July 2026, a decline of 335,000 or 10.8%. An official establishment survey, not a layoff tracker.
evidence.citation: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Current Employment Statistics, series CES5000000001 (All employees, thousands, information, seasonally adjusted).

evidence.title: Job openings, information sector (BLS JOLTS)
evidence.summary: Job openings in the US information sector averaged 224,000 a month in 2022 and 121,000 a month in 2025, and stood at 90,000 in June 2026, against an April 2022 peak of 274,000.
evidence.citation: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, series JTS510000000000000JOL (Job openings, information, total US, seasonally adjusted).

evidence.title: Layoffs and discharges, information sector (BLS JOLTS)
evidence.summary: Official separations in the US information sector were 451,000 in 2022, 399,000 in 2023, 395,000 in 2024 and 447,000 in 2025 — roughly flat across the period, and without the year-to-year collapse reported by tracked-layoff counts over the same span.
evidence.citation: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, series JTU510000000000000LDL (Layoffs and discharges, information, total US, not seasonally adjusted).

evidence.title: Hires, information sector (BLS JOLTS)
evidence.summary: Gross hires in the US information sector fell from 1,270,000 in 2022 to 903,000 in 2025, a decline of 367,000 or 28.9%. The measure counts hiring flows, not layoff announcements.
evidence.citation: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, series JTU510000000000000HIL (Hires, information, total US, not seasonally adjusted).

evidence.title: Tracked technology layoffs (Layoffs.fyi)
evidence.summary: A privately maintained tracker that compiles publicly reported layoff events at technology and startup companies worldwide, revised as new reports arrive. It is not a statistical census. It records 165,269 employees in 2022, 265,660 in 2023, 152,922 in 2024, 122,606 in 2025 and 127,180 between 1 January and 24 August 2026.
evidence.citation: Layoffs.fyi — Tech and Startup Layoff Tracker, per-year pages, retrieved 27 August 2026.

evidence.title: Announced job cuts, technology sector (Challenger, Gray & Christmas)
evidence.summary: A count of announcements of planned job cuts by US-based employers rather than of completed separations; not an official statistic. It reports 133,988 technology-sector cuts announced in 2024, 154,445 in 2025 and 149,023 between January and July 2026 — 67% above the 89,251 announced in the same months of 2025.
evidence.citation: Challenger, Gray & Christmas, Job Cut Announcement Report, July 2026.

evidence.title: Hires rate, total private (BLS JOLTS)
evidence.summary: The seasonally adjusted hires rate for total private employment was 3.7% in June 2026 (preliminary), a full percentage point below its June 2022 level of 4.7%: fewer positions per hundred jobs are being filled each month.
evidence.citation: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, series JTS100000000000000HIR (Hires rate, total private, seasonally adjusted).

evidence.title: Quits rate, information sector (BLS JOLTS)
evidence.summary: The seasonally adjusted quits rate in the US information sector was 1.1% in June 2026 (preliminary), down from 1.9% in June 2022: fewer seats are being vacated by the people already in them.
evidence.citation: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, series JTS510000000000000QUR (Quits rate, information, seasonally adjusted).

evidence.title: Applications per opening (Greenhouse hiring benchmarks)
evidence.summary: Applications received per open role across the reporting platform's customer base rose from 116 in 2022 to 244 in 2025, an increase of 111%. The stated dataset covers over 6,000 companies and over 640 million applications, so it measures one platform's customers rather than the labour market.
evidence.citation: Greenhouse, The Hire Standard: hiring benchmarks report, North America, March 2026.

evidence.title: Seniority mix of software postings (Indeed Hiring Lab)
evidence.summary: Senior-level roles accounted for 69.3% of software development postings and entry-level roles for 4.5% in the first quarter of 2026, measured on one job board's postings rather than on all vacancies.
evidence.citation: Indeed Hiring Lab, The Labor Market Is Tilting Toward Seniority, 23 July 2026.

evidence.title: Employment of young software developers (Stanford Digital Economy Lab)
evidence.summary: In payroll records covering 3.5–5 million workers a month, employment of software developers aged 22–25 fell by close to 20% between its late-2022 peak and September 2025, while employment for older workers in the same occupation did not fall. This is the paper's raw descriptive series for one occupation; its headline regression result — a 16% relative decline for ages 22–25 in AI-exposed occupations, controlling for firm-level shocks — is a different figure and should not be conflated with it.
evidence.citation: Brynjolfsson, E., Chandar, B., & Chen, R. (2025). Canaries in the Coal Mine? Six Facts about the Recent Employment Effects of Artificial Intelligence. Stanford Digital Economy Lab, 13 November 2025.
